extractedText: Get ready for a leadership shakeup at Bulgari, one of the world's most iconic jewelry brands! The Power Shift: A New Era for Bulgari On July 1st, Laura Burdese will step into the role of Chief Executive Officer, taking the reins from Jean-Christophe Babin. This smooth transition is a testament to the brand's strategic vision and a nod to the incredible talent within its ranks. But here's where it gets interesting: Babin isn't going far. He'll continue as Chairman of the Board, CEO of the Bulgari Hotel business unit, and President of the Bulgari Foundation, all while reporting to Stéphane Bianchi, the Group Managing Director of LVMH Watches & Jewelry. "This is a proud moment for me, witnessing the seamless transition from one exceptional leader to another," Bianchi stated, highlighting the collaborative efforts between Burdese and Babin over the past three years to elevate the brand's iconic status. He added, "Laura's appointment is a well-deserved tribute to her contributions, and I'm confident Jean-Christophe will continue to shine in his new roles, bringing his visionary energy to LVMH and its maisons." Burdese, who will also report to Bianchi, brings a wealth of experience to the table. She joined the LVMH Group in 2016 as President and CEO of Acqua di Parma, and later joined Bulgari in 2022 as Vice President of Marketing and Communications. Her career began in the beauty industry, holding brand management positions at Beiersdorf and L'Oréal, before moving into the world of luxury timepieces and jewelry. In 1999, Burdese joined the Swatch Group, where she held various leadership roles, including Brand Director of Calvin Klein Watch & Jewelry and President and CEO of Calvin Klein Watch & Jewelry Co. Ltd. Her expertise in marketing and brand management will undoubtedly be an asset as she takes on the CEO role at Bulgari. Babin, a graduate of HEC Business School in Paris, started his career in 1983 at Procter & Gamble, working in commercial and marketing roles. He later joined Benckiser and Henkel in Italy before becoming CEO of Tag Heuer in 2000. His tenure at Bulgari has been marked by significant achievements, including the expansion of the brand's watchmaking segment and the launch of the Octo Finissimo Ultra COSC, the world's thinnest mechanical watch, which earned Bulgari the inaugural WWD Honor for Watch Brand of the Year in 2024. And this is the part most people miss: Burdese has been a key player in Bulgari's recent expansion. She has worked closely with Babin on the development of the new production facility in Valenza, which was inaugurated in April. This facility, now the largest single-brand jewelry manufacturing site in the world, is a testament to Bulgari's commitment to its Italian heritage and craftsmanship. Under Babin's leadership, Bulgari has also raised the profile of its high jewelry collections through experiential events and fashion shows in Venice, Rome, and Taormina, Sicily. These events have attracted A-list celebrities and ambassadors, including Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, and Lisa from Blackpink. Additionally, Bulgari has expanded its luxury hotel portfolio to nine properties, including locations in Rome, Paris, and Tokyo, with plans for further expansion in Miami and Los Angeles. As Burdese steps into her new role, the future looks bright for Bulgari. With her expertise and the brand's strong foundation, we can expect even more innovative and exciting developments.
